speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the Ministry's assessment of employer awareness of the Tripartite Standard on Unpaid Leave for Unexpected Care Needs, particularly for parents with children born premature, with congenital conditions or as part of multiple births; (b) how many employers have adopted this Standard from 2023 to date; and (c) what further outreach or support is planned to raise adoption of this Standard.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And I thank the Senior Parliamentary of State for his response.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Given that pre-term infants often face prolonged Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) stays and require follow-up appointments, has MOM studied whether the four weeks of unpaid leave per year under the current standard, is sufficient in duration and flexibility?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Next, could MOM also consider publishing a public registry of adopters with opt in, so parents can identify supportive employers?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Lastly, when might MOM intend to review the effectiveness of the TS and what indicators will it use?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Beyond these leave provisions, flexible work arrangements can support all workers, including parents, to more effectively balance their caregiving responsibilities and career aspirations.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Parents can discuss suitable flexible work arrangements with their employers if they require more time to care for their children.
